To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Spi− selection is useful to detect MMC‐induced in vivo deletions and that molecular analyses using PCR and DNA sequencing are useful to evaluate a marginal increase in Spi− mutant frequency in the mouse gpt delta model.

1) Spi− selection is useful to detect deletions induced by treatment with a single dose of MMC, 2) the Spi− selection is also useful to evaluate the statistical significance of a marginal mutant frequency increase observed in the transgenic assays, and 3) the Spi− mutants can be molecularly analyzed to determine the sizes of deletions.
the transgenic mouse model gpt delta can detect in vivo deletions efficiently, using the Spi− assay and molecular analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a transgenic rodent model for the detection of deletions in the mouse.
the development and application of a novel transgenic rodent model, i.e. gpt delta, to detect deletions induced by genotoxic agents.
the use of the transgenic mouse model gpt delta for the detection of deletions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Spi− selection in the transgenic gpt delta mouse is a sensitive assay for detecting deletion mutations in the bone marrow.
the gpt delta transgenic mouse mutation assay can detect a wide variety of gene mutations, including base changes and deletions.

the data presented here do not support the hypothesis of an increased risk of cancer in humans from the consumption of irradiated foods, and that there is no evidence of a genotoxic effect of ionizing radiation at the doses of irradiation currently used for food preservation.

the gpt delta model is a useful model to detect deletions in vivo.
